bundle.guidance:
# Technical Documentation

A reference surface for engineers who are scanning, not reading. Density is a
feature: a page that fits one more paragraph above the fold saves a scroll.

## Principles

1. **Scannable before beautiful.** Every section must be findable from a
   heading alone. Never bury an API name inside prose.
2. **Code is the primary citizen.** Prose exists to explain a snippet, not the
   other way round. If a paragraph can be replaced by a five-line example,
   replace it.
3. **No decoration.** No shadows, no gradients, no illustrations. Rules and
   whitespace carry the structure.

## Layout grid

Single column, `max-width: 46rem`, centred, `--space-xl` between top-level
sections and `--space-lg` between a heading and its body. Do not add a
sidebar or a table of contents column — the hub page is already framed.
Code blocks and tables may break the column to `56rem` when a line would
otherwise wrap.

## Typography

Headings are monospace (`--font-family-heading`, JetBrains Mono) at
`--size-h1` / `--size-h2` / `--size-h3`; they are deliberately small — the
monospace texture, not the size, marks a heading. Body text is Inter at
`--size-body` with `--line-body`. Never go above three heading levels; a
fourth level means the page should be split.

## Colour usage

Text is `--color-text-primary` on `--color-bg-page`. The blue accent
(`--color-brand-primary`) is for links and a single left border on a callout
and nothing else. Status colours mark deprecation (`danger`), beta (`warn`)
and stable (`ok`) badges only. Never colour a heading.

## Charts

Chart.js, bar and line only. One series per colour from the chart palette in
order; never more than four series on one canvas. No pie, no doughnut, no
area fills — an engineer reads exact values, so always print the numbers in a
table underneath the chart.

## Diagrams

Mermaid `flowchart LR` for request paths and `sequenceDiagram` for protocols.
Keep node labels under five words. Do not apply per-node colours; the theme
already matches the palette.

## Components and when to use each

- `callout` — a note, warning or deprecation. At most two per page; a page
  full of callouts has no callouts.
- `api-signature` — one endpoint or function signature above its description.
  Always the first thing in a reference section.
- `param-table` — parameters, fields or environment variables. Prefer it to a
  bulleted list the moment there is more than one attribute per item.
- `code-block` — a labelled snippet with a language tag. Use for anything a
  reader will copy.
- `badge` — stability marker next to a signature, never free-floating.

## Do / don't

- **Do** put the copy-pasteable command before the explanation of it.
- **Do** name the exact version a behaviour changed in.
- **Don't** use emoji, exclamation marks or second-person marketing voice.
- **Don't** centre anything. Everything is left-aligned, including tables.
- **Don't** introduce a colour that is not a token.
